_about: The 2026 Nonfiction Hotlist text. Mirrored from the 2026 Google Drive kit once it is connected. Starts with 25 placeholder projects (Project 01 to Project 25); each takes its real title, and a web address from it, when the Title in its Copysheet is changed.

cover.intro: 20 ambitious nonfiction projects with extraordinary creative potential, each looking for the support to move forward.

welcome.heading: welcome to the nonfiction hotlist
lede: We believe creators and storytellers are the lifeblood of our industry and deserve more pathways to bring their visions to life.
This curated collection represents **20 ambitious projects** that have demonstrated extraordinary creative potential but need support to move forward.
invitation: While funding and distribution remain universal needs for all these projects, we believe there are many ways to help reduce costs and build momentum.
Look through these projects with an eye for how you might contribute. Each page identifies specific needs, from production support to technical expertise to strategic connections.

about.heading: why this matters
why: The marketplace needs ambitious, unusual, and visionary nonfiction projects. When we collaborate as a community, we create new possibilities and counter the risk-aversion of traditional gatekeepers. Every contribution, whether financial investment or in-kind support, generates meaningful momentum, giving creators more leverage.

Supporting these projects strengthens not only their individual journeys but the broader health and vibrancy of our entire nonfiction ecosystem. The hundreds of other remarkable submissions we received confirm the wealth of untapped storytelling potential waiting for champions.
about.selection: Some creators are first-time filmmakers; others are established voices who still face challenges securing support for ambitious work. What unites them is the exceptional quality of their vision.
how: Contact projects directly whose vision inspires you.
Support their 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsorships where available.
Follow their creative journeys across social platforms.
Review each project's How to help section and offer the specific resources they need.
about.close: This document is **meant to be used**. These projects are **meant to be made**. The future of exceptional nonfiction storytelling depends on our collective action.

my-first-phone.title: My First Phone*
my-first-phone.status: In the final stages of production, with an editor on board and the film set to finish by the end of 2027.
my-first-phone.logline: Four kids, their first year with a smartphone, told from inside the phones themselves.
my-first-phone.summary:
For kids today, the defining coming-of-age milestone is no longer a driver's license. It's a phone. My First Phone follows four kids across the United States before, during and after they get their first smartphones.

With every family's full consent and a strict set of safeguards, a custom app records each kid's screen and selfie camera for their entire first year. Nothing is opened until the parents have reviewed it. The four families differ in almost every way that matters.
help: Investors and grants to close the financing gap

untitled-paul-robeson.title: Untitled Paul Robeson
untitled-paul-robeson.status: In production. Early sequences cut with editor Rik Chaubet.
untitled-paul-robeson.logline: A hybrid portrait of Paul Robeson, the stage and screen star who paid a dear price for his political convictions.
untitled-paul-robeson.summary:
This film reclaims the legacy of Paul Robeson, rejecting conventional biography for an immersive character study. Drawing on exclusive access to the Robeson estate archive of more than 50,000 artifacts, it centers his own words, images and music.

Archival material blends with newly filmed tableaux that are not reenactments but poetic reflections on his inner life, shaped by the historical, political and psychological realities he lived through. His legacy still fuels global justice movements today.

fixers.title: Fixers
fixers.status: In production, with post-production to start in November.
fixers.logline: A legendary Mexican fixer brokers cartel access for foreign journalists, and an American filmmaker turns the camera on him.
fixers.summary:
Miguel Angel Vega, 54, is a legend among international journalists in Mexico, the go-to fixer for access to organized crime. In a single day he introduces crews to mothers of the disappeared, talks police into letting cameras onto crime scenes and coaxes narcotraffickers into allowing filming inside a fentanyl lab.

When French journalists arrive in Culiacán wanting narcos with rifles, Miguel doesn't just secure interviews. He stages reality. A rare and at times darkly funny look at the hidden deal-making behind the stories we see, with implications for the filmmaker's own work.

j-is-for-jihad.title: J is for Jihad
j-is-for-jihad.logline: People named Jihad in America gather in a meetup group to share their stories in a country they no longer recognize.
j-is-for-jihad.summary:
J is for Jihad is a hybrid documentary that reclaims a word flattened in the West into a synonym for terror, by returning it to the people who carry it as a name. Jihad means a righteous struggle: striving to be better, or pursuing justice.

In small-town California in 1990, Jihad Jaffer's father gives him a used BMW for his sixteenth birthday, with vanity plates reading 4 JIHAD. Gathered in a meetup group, Jihad and others share stories full of humor and complexity that no stereotype can hold.

captains-don-t-cry.title: Captains Don’t Cry
captains-don-t-cry.status: In the edit, approaching a fine cut.
captains-don-t-cry.logline: An 85-year-old basketball captain leads her team to the National Senior Games, then is suddenly benched.
captains-don-t-cry.summary:
At 85, Sheila Tunstall McKenna doesn't just play basketball. She lives it. For more than 25 years she has been the starting guard of the Connecticut High Fives, a women's team whose players are all in their 80s, with a legacy of competition, friendship and hard-won medals.

With time closing in, the team sets out for one last run at the National Senior Games. Then Sheila is unexpectedly benched, and the decision lands as more than strategy. For the first time in decades she is off the court, facing questions of identity, purpose and what remains.

our-home-is-not-of-this-world.title: Our Home Is Not Of This World
our-home-is-not-of-this-world.status: In post-production and submitting to festivals.
our-home-is-not-of-this-world.logline: A Texas medical examiner who identifies people who die crossing the border wants to retire. No one will replace her.
our-home-is-not-of-this-world.summary:
Our Home Is Not Of This World follows the unseen work of a medical examiner's office in Texas that identifies people who die crossing the border. Dr. Corinne Stern has done this work for more than 20 years. Border Patrol agents lead her to bodies in the brush, and the phones ring with families searching for missing loved ones.

The office has never seen this many cases. It is at its breaking point, and so is Dr. Stern, whose plan to retire puts its future in doubt because the county can't find anyone to replace her.
help: A final round of funding for post-production, festivals and release

the-prison-outside.title: The Prison Outside
the-prison-outside.status: In post-production, finishing a rough cut of Act 1, and aiming to finish the film in 2027.
the-prison-outside.logline: Terrence Graham won his case at the Supreme Court but came of age behind bars. Now he's out. Is life outside another prison?
the-prison-outside.summary:
Arrested at 16 and sentenced to life without parole, Terrence Graham fought his way to the Supreme Court and won. Graham v. Florida ruled that children convicted of crimes other than murder could not be sentenced to life without a chance at parole, changing sentencing for young people across the country.

Yet as thousands were released on his case, Terrence stayed locked up for 20 more years. In February 2024 he walked out of the Duval County Jail at 37. The film follows what freedom looks like after a childhood spent inside.
help: An experienced producer to help with festivals and distribution
Color grading, sound design and mixing

shiitake.title: Shiitake
shiitake.status: First shoot complete. Fundraising to finish production.
shiitake.logline: After nearly dying of cancer, a young woman sets out to learn from Japan's last shiitake masters before their craft disappears.
shiitake.summary:
In the mountains of Japan, a dwindling community of aging farmers keeps alive a 2,000-year-old tradition: growing shiitake on felled oak logs. The slow, physical work sustains far more than mushrooms. The forests these farmers tend hold hillsides together, catch monsoon rains and feed a cycle of water from mountain canopy to sea.

As younger generations leave for the cities and the climate shifts, that balance is coming apart. After nearly dying of cancer, a young woman sets out to learn from the last shiitake masters while there is still time.

hares-on-the-mountain.title: Hares on the Mountain
hares-on-the-mountain.status: Moving from development into production, after three scouting trips.
hares-on-the-mountain.logline: As coal fades and tech moves in, a homecoming film asks who decides the future of Appalachia.
hares-on-the-mountain.summary:
Hares on the Mountain is a personal and social film about the future of the Appalachian coal fields, from the spread of data centers to Indigenous efforts to bring bison back to former mine lands. It spends time with communities living on the coal beds of West Virginia, Kentucky and Virginia.

Unwilling to dismiss the people left behind by extractive industry, the film asks what this region could do if it were allowed self-determination. An environmental allegory about community ties and the mountain as a lasting site of struggle.

who-goes-fascist.title: Who Goes Fascist
who-goes-fascist.status: Characters secured and pre-interviews done. Seeking funding.
who-goes-fascist.logline: Not whether it could happen here, but whether it could happen to you.
who-goes-fascist.summary:
In April 1967, high school history teacher Ron Jones was asked how ordinary Germans could have let the Holocaust happen. Rather than lecture, he decided to show his students.

He introduced a movement called The Third Wave, built on discipline, community and action. Within days his students were saluting, reporting on classmates who didn't comply and shutting out anyone who objected. The five-day experiment spiraled beyond anyone's control and left scars that persist nearly sixty years later.

the-vodou-project.title: The Vodou Project
the-vodou-project.status: In production. One final reporting trip to Haiti remains.
the-vodou-project.logline: A Haitian-American journalist travels the African diaspora to learn why he was taught to fear Vodou.
the-vodou-project.summary:
The Vodou Project follows Haitian-American journalist Baudelaire Ceus as he investigates the spiritual tradition he grew up fearing. Reporting across Haiti, Benin, Cuba, New Orleans and the wider African diaspora, the series traces Vodou from its West African roots through slavery, the Haitian Revolution and migration.

Baudelaire talks with practitioners, historians and his own family to understand how a tradition that helped enslaved people keep their identity and fight for liberation came to be feared.

border-hacker.title: Border Hacker
border-hacker.status: Most reporting complete, from more than a decade following Axel. Episodes outlined.
border-hacker.logline: A deported New Yorker uses his hacking skills to get back to the US and is caught in a web of traffickers and corrupt priests.
border-hacker.summary:
In August 2026, Axel Kirschner told an immigration court that if he were deported again he would almost certainly be murdered, by a famous Catholic priest. The judge called his case not credible.

Levi Vonk knows Axel, and knows the priest. Adapted from his book Border Hacker, this series follows Axel, an Afro-Latino stateless migrant and computer hacker, on a decade-long journey through Mexico, where his skills ensnare him with human traffickers, corrupt priests and guerrillas eager to use them.

power.title: Power
power.status: Editing toward an assembly cut. Andrew Pilkington (Being Heumann) has joined as consulting producer.
power.logline: The US power wheelchair soccer team heads to the World Cup, until a sudden death leaves them competing through grief.
power.summary:
Power follows the US Power Soccer National Team at a defining moment, through five athletes: Drew, Natalie, Jordan, Zach and Riley. In custom wheelchairs built for competition, they tear across the court and drive the ball into the goal with a joystick and centripetal force.

Each found the sport by a different path, and through it found fierce competition, deep friendship and love. Heading to the FIPFA Powerchair Football World Cup, the team is shaken by a sudden death and must compete through devastating grief.
help: $30,000 to $50,000 in near-term funding to complete a rough cut
A lead producer and an LA-based production company
Connections to brand partners and distributors

meant-to-be-maddie.title: Meant to Be Maddie
meant-to-be-maddie.status: At rough cut, aiming to premiere in late 2027 or early 2028.
meant-to-be-maddie.logline: A decade in the life of a North Carolina trans teenager and the family behind her, as anti-trans backlash grows.
meant-to-be-maddie.summary:
Maddie was eight when North Carolina's 2016 bathroom bill put trans kids at the center of national debate and forced her into the only single-stall bathroom at her school. When the bill was rescinded, it felt like her family was part of a growing wave of acceptance.

Since then, anti-trans legislation has multiplied, with hundreds of bills filed across the country, many aimed at trans youth. Filmed over ten years, Meant to Be Maddie is an intimate and funny coming-of-age story, made with the unwavering support of her family.

young-lions.title: Young Lions
young-lions.status: In early pre-production. Sizzle reel, deck and budget complete.
young-lions.logline: South African surfer Paul "Chow" Sampson fights his way back to the elite, to open the sport for the next generation.
young-lions.summary:
Paul "Chow" Sampson was six and homeless, sheltering under the beach overhangs of Muizenberg, when youth surf coach Shafiek Khan pulled him into the water. Shafiek has been his manager, mentor and closest thing to a father ever since.

Paul became one of South Africa's most accomplished Black surfers in a sport whose professional ranks remain overwhelmingly white, then lost his place when he could no longer afford the chase. With Shafiek beside him, he fights his way back.

a-tender-weapon.title: A Tender Weapon
a-tender-weapon.status: In post-production, raising funds to reach picture lock.
a-tender-weapon.logline: Cleve Jones turned grief into the AIDS Memorial Quilt. Decades later, he comes out of retirement to organize again.
a-tender-weapon.summary:
In the early years of the AIDS epidemic, people were dying at staggering rates and the federal government largely looked away. Cleve Jones, then in his twenties in San Francisco's Castro, asked what it would take to make the rest of the country care. His answer was the AIDS Memorial Quilt, which turned a generation's grief into political force.

Decades later, as sweeping healthcare cuts threaten millions of Americans, Cleve comes out of retirement to build a new movement, asking whether collective pain can still move a country to act.

love-and-justice.title: Love & Justice
love-and-justice.status: 22 interviews complete. Editing begins this fall.
love-and-justice.logline: A Baptist preacher and a Jewish secretary from the Bronx quietly broke the law to expand human dignity.
love-and-justice.summary:
A Southern Baptist preacher from Texas and a Jewish secretary from the Bronx gave each other permission to break the law in the name of conscience. Over 27 years at Judson Memorial Church in Greenwich Village, Rev. Howard Moody and Arlene Carmen connected 500,000 women to safe abortion care before Roe v. Wade.

They distributed illegal AIDS treatments before the government would act and fought to decriminalize prostitution before sex workers had advocates. Theirs was one of the most consequential and least known partnerships in American civil rights history.

the-dead-zone.title: The Dead Zone
the-dead-zone.status: In post-production, raising the last $50,000 to finish.
the-dead-zone.logline: Four insiders across the South fight to fix pretrial detention, where two people die every day.
the-dead-zone.summary:
Every day, two people die in pretrial detention, the stretch between arrest and conviction. From the Mississippi Delta to the Kentucky Bluegrass, The Dead Zone brings humanity to one of America's most overlooked crises.

Filmed over four years, it follows four people whose lives meet inside this hidden system: an accused man who waited six years in jail for trial, a public defender, a judge and a district attorney. Together they show how poverty, politics and power collide between arrest and trial, and what reform could look like.
help: $50,000 in finishing funds for color, sound mix, music and the online edit
Executive producers, sales agents and distributors

crystal-city.title: Crystal City
crystal-city.status: Early production. Over $200,000 raised in grants, with a rough cut expected in summer 2027.
crystal-city.logline: Barred from the cheer squad by a racist quota, a Texas teenager sparks a 1969 student walkout that remakes her town's politics.
crystal-city.summary:
It's 1969 in Crystal City, Texas, and sixteen-year-old Diana Palacios, the daughter of migrant farmworkers, just wants to be a cheerleader. Mexican American students make up 85 percent of the school, but an unofficial quota allows only one Chicana on the squad, and Diana is turned away.

Her best friend Severita Lara sees that the squad was never the real problem. The same rules run the whole town. The students write a list of demands, the school board ignores them, and in December 1969 nearly 2,000 students walk out over seventeen days.

A fight over a cheerleading squad becomes a lesson in civic power: who gets heard, who gets counted, and what happens when a community shut out of the process organizes itself.

kamnop-a-treasure-is-waiting-for-you.title: Kamnop: A Treasure is Waiting For You
kamnop-a-treasure-is-waiting-for-you.status: Late development, starting production. The first filming trip in Cambodia is complete.
kamnop-a-treasure-is-waiting-for-you.logline: A daughter and mother travel from Colorado to Cambodia in search of treasure buried in the first days of the Khmer Rouge genocide.
kamnop-a-treasure-is-waiting-for-you.summary:
Kanika, 70, lives a quiet, withdrawn life in suburban Colorado, haunted by a recurring dream in which the Buddha tells her a kamnop, a treasure, awaits her. At 16 she fled Cambodia during the Khmer Rouge regime, remembering her father burying gold and jewels at their home before she left. Five of her siblings and both parents were killed in the genocide.

Her daughter Kanitha, 39, born in the U.S., has spent years trying to understand her mother's past. When she learns the childhood home still stands, occupied by a stranger and threatened with demolition, she convinces her mother the dream might be true.

What begins as a treasure hunt becomes a search for what one generation passes to the next.

ski-the-wong-way.title: Ski The Wong Way
ski-the-wong-way.status: Late development. About three quarters financed, with Telefilm and Creative BC funding in place.
ski-the-wong-way.logline: Freestyle skiing icon Wayne Wong, grieving the loss of his wife, sets out for his 65th ski season in Park City, Utah.
ski-the-wong-way.summary:
Ski the Wong Way is the untold story of Wayne Wong, the Chinese Canadian from Vancouver who became the unlikely face of hot-dog skiing in the 1970s and 80s. His signature move, the Wongbanger, hung on bedroom walls across the era, and Powder Magazine named him one of the most influential skiers of all time.

Now, still grieving the sudden loss of his wife Karen, Wayne sets out from Reno for his 65th season as ambassador for Deer Valley Resort, despite worries from his doctor, his daughters and his 90-something mother.

With rare access to Wayne, his family and the ski world, and a trove of archival footage, the film is a romp through the roots of the sport and a love story about a man who dared to be himself.

a-banner-year.title: A Banner Year
a-banner-year.status: In post-production, with a rough cut expected by the end of January.
a-banner-year.logline: A year inside the Baltimore Banner, a nonprofit newsroom built from scratch to prove that local journalism can still be saved.
a-banner-year.summary:
Every week, two American newspapers shut down. In Baltimore, after a hedge fund bought the Sun, a local philanthropist started the Baltimore Banner as a nonprofit alternative. A Banner Year follows its newsroom through the year it grows up: a city hall reporter covering a tight mayoral race, an investigative team chasing decades of covered-up abuse at a megachurch, and the collapse of the Key Bridge.

With access no other cameras had inside a newsroom of more than 100 journalists, the film follows editor-in-chief Kimi Yoshino and her reporters as they build something new while the industry around them shrinks, all the way to a Pulitzer Prize for local reporting. It asks whether this experiment is the future of local news or proof that it can't be saved.
help: Help shaping an impact campaign with nonprofit newsrooms
Introductions to funders who support journalism, democracy and documentary
Finishing funds for the edit, color and sound

ash-street-jail.title: Ash Street Jail
ash-street-jail.status: In post-production, working through story structure, with a possible additional shoot in 2027.
ash-street-jail.logline: Inside the oldest operating jail in the US, open since 1888. A new sheriff wants to close it. Can he?
ash-street-jail.summary:
The Ash Street Jail opened in 1888 and still holds pretrial defendants in a small Massachusetts city. A sheriff elected on reform wants to close it, but the political establishment has ignored him.

Inmates struggle to cope in cramped, decaying cells, and the jail has the highest suicide rate of any Massachusetts county jail. Still, some feel deeply tied to its walls. One lives in the same cell his late father once did.
help: A producer with experience in stories about incarceration and the justice system
Distribution through a news outlet such as Op-Docs, The New Yorker or the Boston Globe
